newsitem.title: USA: Spier withdraws offer for Video Lottery.
newsitem.headline: Spier withdraws offer for Video Lottery.

text.p: Investor William Spier, a shareholder in Video Lottery Technologies Inc, said Tuesday he has withdrawn his offer to buy the company for $6 per share.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Spier cited the continued refusal of the company's board of directors to consider the proposal seriously.
Spier is a director of the company and leader of a group that already owns 14.4 percent of Video Lottery.
In the filing, Spier also cited the majority of the board's "apparent stubborn commitment" to raising unreasonable obstacles to the proposed transaction.
Spier said he waited two months for the company to respond to his proposal and that the board had yet to provide him with any basis for concluding that the proposal would be reviewed fairly.
On January 6, Video Lottery said it wanted to evaluate the offer made by Spier and his group before making a final decision.

Video Lottery had formed a special committee to the board of directors to review the proposal that included an offer to buy another 20 percent of Video Lottery's common stock at $6 per share immediately upon the signing of the agreement.
Video Lottery of Atlanta, Ga., provides terminals, software and services to the video lottery market. With about 10.7 million shares outstanding, the Spier bid was worth about $64.2 million.
In late afternoon trade, Video Lottery was down 1/4 at $3-3/4 per share on the Nasdaq market.
